origins: Moves, divorce, immigration, a church split, a difference in temperament or beliefs, or years of being the odd one out can leave a person feeling that no group is truly theirs. We may feel like visitors in our own lives. The longer it lasts, the more “nowhere” seems to be the answer.
teaches: Peter writes, “You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession.” Paul says, “You are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household.” “God settles the lonely in families.” John says that “to all who did receive Him… He gave the right to become children of God.” Belonging with God is settled by His choice, not by any group’s acceptance. From that secure place, you can look for and build human belonging.
self_statements: There is no place for me.
I always feel like a guest.
Every group already has its own.
I will always be on the outside.
No one would notice if I left.
errors: Treating some experiences of exclusion as universal.
Predicting I will never find a place.
Feeling out of place and concluding I am.
questions: Where have I felt closest to belonging, even briefly?
What did those places have in common?
What do I want from a group: acceptance, shared values, friendship, purpose?
What does Scripture say about my place with God?
What small step could I take to join or build community?
Whom might I welcome who feels the same?
truth: I belong to God by His choice, and He has made me part of His household. I can look for human communities that fit, take small steps, and help build belonging for others.
hw_truths: I am chosen and God’s own possession.
I am a member of God’s household.
God settles the lonely in families.
I have the right to be His child.
log: Each week, note one place or person where you felt welcome.
actions: Write where and with whom you felt at home.
Join something recurring for four weeks.
prayer: Father, You have made me Your own. Settle me in a community where I can give and receive. Help me welcome others who feel like outsiders. Amen.
hw_questions: Where have I felt at home?
What do I want from a group?
What does God say about my place?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am chosen and belong to God.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I don't belong anywhere.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
